title: Choose the Right Instance Family
description: Match workload scenarios with the optimal EC2 instance family.
problemStatement:
For each scenario, select the most suitable EC2 instance family (General purpose, Compute‑optimised, Memory‑optimised, Accelerated computing) and explain briefly why.

1. A stateless containerised microservice that receives variable traffic throughout the day.
2. A high‑frequency trading application that needs the fastest possible single‑threaded CPU performance.
3. An in‑memory Redis cache holding 200 GB of data.
4. A nightly batch job that processes video files with no deadline and can be interrupted.
5. A 3D rendering farm used by a film studio.
hints: Consider bursting requirements, memory size, CPU speed, and tolerance to interruption.
Spot instances can be used with any family, but some jobs are more fault‑tolerant.
solutionCode:
1. **Burstable (T‑series)** – The variable traffic benefits from CPU credits to handle spikes without paying for constant high performance.
2. **Compute‑optimised (C‑series)** – These offer high clock speeds and a high CPU‑to‑memory ratio for single‑threaded performance.
3. **Memory‑optimised (R‑series)** – Redis holds data entirely in memory; 200 GB requires a memory‑optimised instance like r5.4xlarge.
4. **Any family with Spot Instances** – Since the job is fault‑tolerant and not time‑critical, Spot instances (often using compute‑optimised or general purpose) can save up to 90%.
5. **Accelerated computing (G‑series)** – GPU instances are built for graphics rendering and video processing.
